answer: Agents selling ocean surveys, island maps or services detecting ivory must obtain an epoch ticket. Its input hashes the public beacon, epoch and agent key. The agent evaluates a verifiable delay function; validators check its proof and reject wrong, stale or already-used tickets. Different keys require different evaluations, so extra aliases each consume processor time and energy. Parallel machines shorten the swarm's wait but do not share solutions. Security assumes no faster evaluation shortcut and a per-ticket cost above the gain from an extra seat.
